hero.lead: An island nation of 530,000 in the Indian Ocean, where visitors earn four fifths of export income, public debt reached 129% of GDP in 2025, and a $500 million sukuk was repaid in full in April 2026.

capital.heading: A tourism economy, through its hardest repayment year.

register.name: Sovereign sukuk, repaid at maturity
register.detail: Maldives Monetary Authority · settlement completed 2 April 2026, with the associated coupon payments · met from official reserves and the Sovereign Development Fund
register.note: US$524.68 million paid in all, according to the Manohar Parrikar IDSA
register.text: The US$500 million sovereign sukuk, settled in full at maturity by the Maldives Monetary Authority on 2 April 2026 from official reserves and the Sovereign Development Fund. Its repayment concerns the public finances as a whole: official reserves fell from $1.3 billion in March to $717.9 million in April 2026, according to the World Bank.

register.name: Maldives Emergency Support for Critical Services Project
register.detail: World Bank · approved 4 May 2026 · principal US$40 million · reallocated from existing projects to support fuel imports, according to Atoll Times
register.note: With the ADB’s US$50 million emergency loan, US$90 million arranged for fuel supplies and related services
register.text: World Bank financing approved in May 2026 to support fuel imports, for the purpose the ADB names for its own emergency loan: keeping power and water running. Imported fuel produces 94% of the country’s electricity and runs the desalination plants that supply drinking water, so it bears on the energy and water standards.

register.name: Toward Risk-Aware and Climate-resilienT communities (TRACT)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · SAP050 · grant approved 3 July 2025 (B.42) · accredited entity UNEP · to July 2030 · 15% disbursed
register.note: US$248,570 of co-financing in kind; total project value US$25.2 million
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant that strengthens climate services and impact-based multi-hazard early warning across the Maldives, so that communities on its dispersed islands can prepare for sea-level rise and extreme weather. Earlier warning protects homes and livelihoods, which bears on the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Atoll Education Development Project, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · Global Partnership for Education Multiplier grant · announced 30 October 2024 · P181581 · total project financing $12.775 million
register.note: The original project, approved in September 2022, carries a $4.5 million IDA grant and a $4.5 million IDA credit
register.text: A grant from the Global Partnership for Education, through the World Bank, added to a project that improves teacher effectiveness and student learning at secondary level in mathematics, science and English, with special focus on the outer atolls. It reaches nearly all of the 100 target schools and serves the education standard.

register.name: Energy Security Emergency Assistance Project
register.detail: ADB · 60245-001 · approved 11 August 2026 · signed 16 August 2026, with the State Trading Organisation · 1.0% a year · 40 years, including 10 years’ grace · ordinary capital resources
register.note: Complements US$40 million from the World Bank for the same purpose
register.text: An ADB emergency loan that funds critical diesel imports to keep power and water running, and also covers food and health-care logistics, the movement of people and cargo between islands and waste management, after the Middle East conflict raised fuel prices and reduced tourist arrivals. Imported fuel produces 94% of the country’s electricity and runs the desalination plants that supply drinking water, so it serves the energy and water standards.

register.name: Strengthening Fiscal Management and Sustainability Program
register.detail: AIIB · P000815 · sovereign results-based loan · approved 28 August 2024 · implementation Q3 2024 to Q2 2027 · interest buy-down of about US$2.74 million from the Special Fund Window
register.note: Supports the policy actions under ADB’s US$18.7 million policy-based grant of September 2023
register.text: A results-based loan from the AIIB to the Republic of Maldives to strengthen fiscal sustainability and promote climate-resilient investment, with results areas in green taxation and in climate mitigation and adaptation. It finances the public finances as a whole; the Special Fund grant reduces its interest rate by 100 basis points.

register.name: Currency swap facility
register.detail: Reserve Bank of India · INR 30 billion (Rs 3,000 crore) · signed October 2024 · first drawdown approved April 2026 under the SAARC Currency Swap Framework, 2024 to 2027
register.note: Drawn as the US$400 million swap was settled; the framework includes concessional interest rate terms
register.text: A rupee swap line from the Reserve Bank of India, signed during the President’s visit to New Delhi in October 2024 and drawn from April 2026, as the earlier US$400 million swap was repaid. It supports the reserves and the public finances as a whole.

register.name: 500 social housing units in Malé
register.detail: China International Development Cooperation Agency · project minutes signed in Beijing, 21 to 22 April 2026 · interest-free facility extended by China
register.note: No amount published; further grant aid cooperation was discussed alongside the signing
register.text: Minutes signed with the China International Development Cooperation Agency for 500 social housing units in Malé, to be financed through an interest-free facility extended by China. It serves the shelter standard, the standard furthest from reach in the Maldives.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2020
items.text: Coral atolls, resorts and reefs: visitors earn four fifths of export income.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 19% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Coconut palms and mangroves on low coral islands.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Less than 300 square kilometres of land across a vast ocean territory.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: A fifth of the land farmed: coconuts, fruit and vegetables, with most food imported.

items.name: Vaadhoo Green Farm
items.text: A community-led hydroponic farm on Vaadhoo, powered by rooftop solar and rainwater harvesting, where 18 women were trained in hydroponic farming; it can grow up to 600 kilograms of cucumbers and 400 kilograms of leafy greens a harvest, for an estimated income of MVR 80,000 a month.

items.name: Housing Development Finance Corporation (HDFC Maldives)
items.text: The Maldives’ only dedicated housing finance institution, owned by the Government, the ADB, IFC and HDFC Bank, which lends for home construction, purchase and improvement, with conventional, Islamic and Lite financing, and has funded more than 24,000 housing units and created more than 6,000 homeowners.

items.name: Syllabi
items.text: A Maldivian education technology company, founded in 2018, whose exam practice platform gives O-Level and A-Level students revision notes, practice questions and instant feedback on phones, tablets and laptops, and is used by more than 70 schools across the Maldives.
